aspects.says: A borrowed channel always goes back to the pool, even when the work done with it fails, and a channel that has dropped is discarded rather than handed out.
basis: section:3.1.3 Advanced Usage with Connection Pool

aspects.says: A client connects its channel, sends a request with a timeout, treats a null response as no answer, and disconnects when done.
aspects.reason: it needs a live peer to answer, and a graded run is offline; org.jpos.iso.ISOClient does not exist in jPOS 2.1.7, and the null-means-no-answer idea is practised on page 4

aspects.says: A connection pool exists to keep channels connected between uses, so a borrowed channel is connected once and reused rather than reconnected for every request.
basis: section:3.1.3 Advanced Usage with Connection Pool

aspects.says: Secure communication wraps the channel in TLS, configured with a keystore and a truststore.
aspects.reason: it needs certificates and a live TLS peer, which a graded offline run has not; in jPOS 2.1.7 NACChannel has no keystore setters, TLS comes from a socket factory
